core_obligations: Set up the parameters: let d be the degree of the division algebra over Q and let lambda be the highest weight of the standard representation, so that its powers represent the character group (proof lines 548-549).

Identify the Brauer classes: the Tits algebras of the Q-form and of the real form at the weight lambda^i are Brauer equivalent to the i-fold tensor powers of D and of the real division algebra, respectively (proof lines 550-552).

The forward implication: if the algebra is R-universal then taking i = 1 and using that the real Tits algebra is either R or the quaternions, the division-algebra description of R-universality forces D to be Q or a quaternion algebra that does not split over R (proof lines 554-556).

The converse: if D is Q or a non-split quaternion algebra then D squared is Brauer equivalent to Q, so the base change of every Tits algebra is a division algebra (R for even i, H for odd i), and the division-algebra description gives R-universality (proof lines 558-563).
proof_roadmap: 先算出 Tits 代数：lambda^i 处的 Tits 代数与 D 的 i 次张量幂 Brauer 等价。
正向取 i=1，由实 Tits 代数是 R 或四元数除法代数得到 D 的形状；反向由 D^2 与 Q Brauer 等价，说明每个 Tits 代数在张量 R 后仍是除法代数，从而 R-universal。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the classification of R-universality for the special linear Lie algebra over a central division algebra (author prop at source lines 541-545): it holds exactly when the division algebra is Q itself or a quaternion algebra that does not split over R. The proof (source lines 547-564) computes the Tits algebras at the powers of the highest weight of the standard representation as the tensor powers of the division algebra (proof lines 550-552), then reads the two implications off the author's division-algebra description of R-universality, using that the real Tits algebra is either R or the quaternions in the forward direction and that the square of a quaternion algebra is Brauer trivial in the converse (proof lines 554-563). The whole content is the Brauer-class computation and the parity split. H2.
